newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks end with strong gains, seen bullish.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks end with strong gains, seen bullish.

text.p: Greek shares kicked off the week with gains of 2.61 percent or 32.30 points on Monday with brokers saying the bourse would continue to advance on expectations of easing inflation and interest rates.

"The market will continue to be bullish. All corrections during February have occured intra-day but the index has managed to close higher. This shows that the market is on a strong uptrend," said broker Nickos Stylianou at Capital Securities.

During the weekend, Greece's National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papantoniou predicted that inflation would fall to 5.0 percent by summer and interest rates would drop to single-digits in the next few months.
January CPI inflation fell to 6.8 percent year-on-year from 7.3 percent in December based on the revised index.
On Monday, OTE gained 155 drachmas at 5,860 recording a new high since its last peak at 5,800 drachmas on February 11.
The Athens general share index settled 2.61 percent or 32.30 points higher at 1270.74 points from Friday's 1238.44, after opening at 1246.65.
Gainers led losers 187 to 54 with 9 issues unchanged on 250 traded. Turnover was 15.2 billion drachmas on volume of 5.2 million shares.

All sectoral indices rose. Construction stocks led the rally, climbing 3.70 percent. Banks followed with a rise of 3.15 percent and industrials gained 1.75 percent. Leasing shares rose 1.53 and investment shares closed 1.72 percent higher.
